items.title: Prepare the corrective successor's functional and security contract
items.detail: A clean install of the exact public wheel with the CLI-recommended [mcp] extra cannot start serve because Ladybug is absent. Dormant legacy MCP modules can build an unauthenticated arbitrary-host eight-tool server outside the production four-tool loopback/token contract. The wheel also contains a personalized YAML resource and dormant undeclared GLiNER path. The source candidate adds the complete [serve] aggregate plus an identical [mcp] compatibility alias, executes the standalone Ladybug graph boundary, both live server installs, and JSON-LD export from clean wheels, fails legacy MCP construction closed, retires the GLiNER dependency/manifest/executable path behind a deprecated fail-closed import tombstone, and removes the resource. It also intentionally replaces the client-derived budget API names with CORPUS_BUDGET_SECONDS and the corpus suite key without aliases, while preserving the marginalia pilot command and changing its report basename to pilot-log.YYYY-MM-DD.json. These are privacy-neutralizing public compatibility breaks, so downstream callers and report consumers must migrate. The public 0.0.40 wheel is immutable and must stay prerelease; its then-authorized successor 0.0.41 closed these defects but was later made non-promotable by separate native Windows lifecycle failures.

items.title: Publish the authorized v0.0.42 immutable successor
items.detail: The real native Windows run made immutable 0.0.41 non-promotable. Its lifecycle writer assumes os.fchmod exists; its Windows byte-range lock covers a PID payload byte that status/stop must read; and its venv launcher PID can differ from the runtime PID that owns the lifecycle lock. Source repairs guard the optional chmod, move the lock byte beyond the bounded payload, and bind readiness to the lock-owning runtime PID. A later full interactive run exposed and repaired the remaining keyless private-LAN LiteLLM placeholder gate. The assigned-version live judge gate then exposed missing candidate descriptions in the optional cluster-select prompt; bounded description parity closed it without changing thresholds or fallback policy, and the repeated pairwise/cluster gate passed 10/10 on both paths with every precision guard green. Version 0.0.42 is explicitly authorized and assigned to those repairs. Diagnostic and local runs are not release evidence; promotion requires the complete exact-source, exact-wheel, distribution, Linux Docker+tmux, and real interactive Windows PowerShell 5.1 gates, including the supported transition from public 0.0.41. No run can promote 0.0.41. Version 0.0.42 was then published as a prerelease from its source tag. Its release asset was replaced in place after publication, so the currently downloadable wheel is not the wheel originally uploaded. This row is done for publication only: no native Windows PowerShell 5.1 lifecycle evidence exists for the 0.0.42 artifact, and the immutable 0.0.41 and 0.0.40 artifacts remain non-promotable.

items.title: Per-step LLM config + LiteLLM provider substrate
items.detail: The flat llm: block became per-step: an llm.defaults baseline plus independent llm.extraction / llm.judge / llm.curator / llm.relation_curator / llm.ask override blocks, each a StepLLM (provider, api_base, model, api_key_env, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, presence_penalty, enable_thinking, and a step-only system_prompt) that inherits any unset field from defaults — so extraction can run a big local model while judge/curator calls run something cheaper. LLMConfig.resolved(step) merges step onto defaults; the config-write path deep-merges so a one-field step patch never clobbers the rest of the block, and the seeded step defaults (extraction enable_thinking=False, judge/curator temperature=0.2) survive a patch instead of reverting to the baseline. The provider substrate migrated to LiteLLM: OpenAICompatProvider was removed and replaced by LiteLLMProvider (lazy import litellm, model string carries the provider prefix e.g. openai/<model>, top_k/min_p/enable_thinking via extra_body, key read from env at call time), behind an optional [litellm] extra; StubLLM stays for CI. A new POST /api/v1/llm/test endpoint (loopback-gated, stub short-circuit, bounded GET {api_base}/models, SSRF-checked, api_key_env namespace-validated, never echoes the secret) backs a per-card Test button in the UI. Config writes stay loopback-only regardless of allow_remote; allow_remote only widens where the server may POST. Per-step LLM changes apply live; embedding provider/model/dimension changes return applied:reembed and run as their own explicit vectors-only job (see 'Configurable embedding model'), never an auto-restart.

items.title: Configurable embedding model + vectors-only kg reembed
items.detail: The embedding side caught up to the per-step LLM work: EmbeddingConfig went from a two-field provider/model stub to a typed, extra=forbid block (provider, api_base, model, api_key_env, allow_remote, dimension) mirroring LLMDefaults, and the substrate gained a LiteLLM path. get_provider now resolves three lanes — fastembed (the local BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 default), an external OpenAI-compatible endpoint via LiteLLM (LM Studio / ollama / vLLM / OpenAI, openai/<model> prefix + explicit api_base, key read from env at call time, never stored or logged), and StubEmbedder for CI — each asserting the returned vector is exactly the configured dimension so a wrong-width model fails loud instead of silently corrupting cosine. Vector width is no longer hardcoded 384: the Ladybug schema parameterizes the DOUBLE[dim] column, records embedding_dim on the schema-metadata node, and a startup dim-guard (verify_embedding_dim → EmbeddingDimMismatch, exit 14) refuses to open a graph whose stored width disagrees with config, naming `kg reembed` as the remedy. A graph built before the embedding_dim column existed is migrated in place at open — an idempotent ALTER adds the column (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never alters an existing table) and it is accepted with no recorded width until a reembed records one — so a pre-existing vault keeps working without a forced rebuild. Because Ladybug columns are fixed-width, a model change can't update in place — so a new vectors-only reembed recomputes embeddings from the existing graph's stored text WITHOUT re-running LLM extraction: it reads the live graph via a raw handle, bootstraps a fresh graph at the new width, copies nodes (recomputing each vector) then edges, health-checks, and atomic-swaps. A gating correctness fix underpins it: primitives embed title\ncontent while a Claim embeds its bare content, so one shared embedding_text_for(node) helper routes both write sites AND the reembed engine, preventing a Claim from being embedded twice. The job is explicit-only — a config PATCH that changes provider/model/dimension returns applied:reembed and mutates nothing; the heavy run fires only on an explicit action: CLI `kg reembed`, or POST /api/v1/embedding/reembed (loopback-gated, 409 while draining, runs on a real OS thread that waits out any in-flight ingest write before reading so no commit is lost to the swap) with GET /api/v1/embedding/reembed/status for progress, plus POST /api/v1/embedding/test mirroring the LLM Test button (loopback, SSRF + api_key_env namespace checks, never echoes the secret). Verified end-to-end with real fastembed (lossless same-model reembed, Claim-vector invariant, dim-assert) and against a real LM Studio endpoint (768-dim nomic reembed, non-loopback refused unless allow_remote).

items.title: ADR 0013 — durable candidate ledger and commit-plan boundary

Converting the remaining legacy review file into a pure ledger projection is future product cleanup, not unfinished core boundary work.

items.title: Entity alias resolution quality — organization/name variants
items.detail: The two-vault guardrail exposed a generic resolver gap: exact-title and embedding-band judge passes kept safe behavior, but they missed same-organization publisher variants such as Ballantine/Ballantine Books and Houghton Mifflin/Houghton Mifflin Company in the LOTR publication-history slice. The fix keeps merge authority with the existing conservative LLMMergeJudge: legal/publisher suffix matching is recall-only, adding obvious alias pairs to the candidate set when embeddings miss them, while same-type, edge-connected guards, merge confidence, and the judge's distinct verdict still control graph writes. Negative tests prove non-suffix token overlap such as Apple/Apple Records stays below the band and is not judged or merged. Live LOTR reset/reingest now supersedes Ballantine -> Ballantine Books and Houghton Mifflin -> Houghton Mifflin Company while committing only the canonical publisher nodes; live CoP reset/reingest still passes the original SDLC quality guardrail with no queue errors, no plural taxonomy leakage, and no structural title noise.

items.title: Incremental re-ingest + continuous folder monitoring (ADR 0023/0024/0025) + live-run remediation
items.detail: Re-ingesting an edited file is now cheap and default-on, and any local directory can feed the graph unattended. Three ADRs plus a 2026-07-02 live-run remediation series (13 fixes, F1–F13, from the first real production run on the `demo-vault` vault). Incremental partition (ADR 0023) + sub-chunk diff (ADR 0024) are now driven by a typed `IngestConfig` and DEFAULT ON: `ingest.incremental` / `ingest.subchunk` in `marginalia.yaml` (writable via `PATCH /api/v1/config`); `MARGINALIA_INCREMENTAL_INGEST` / `MARGINALIA_SUBCHUNK_INGEST` are two-way env overrides (`1` forces on, `0` forces off, unset defers to config); library callers without a vault config inherit the ON default. On re-ingest, unchanged Blocks skip re-extraction by content-hash, and a changed Block is narrowed by difflib to only the edited hunks. Crash-resume: an interrupted run resumes from the durable candidate ledger via `has_open_run` (resume bypass) with `close_stale_runs` clearing dead runs, so incremental partitioning does not lose an in-flight ingest. The reconcile pass — extracted into `_reconcile_removals` and now run on BOTH the normal commit path AND the zero-candidate early return (F6: pure deletions finally detach) — supersedes corrected facts, detaches removed ones, and resurrects reverted ones: detach is sentence-unit + attribution-survival aware (F9: an `OrphanDiff` line-diffs each orphan Block against the union of current Blocks so a fact whose line merely MOVED is not detached; only a genuinely-vanished anchored line detaches), and resurrection (F7) restores a `_superseded`/`_detached` claim whose content returns, through a mint-path merge leg and a deterministic `resurrect_reverted_claims` sweep. Corrections are recency-aware (F8, ADR 0022 addendum): every LLM-minted Claim carries `asserted_at` = the source file's mtime at ingest (folder watcher's copy2 preserves mtime), the supersede prefilter drops any existing claim asserted later than the incoming source, and the resurrection legs are recency-gated so restoring an old backup never resurrects facts corrected later. Continuous folder monitoring (ADR 0025): a global, multi-vault polling watch loop (`server/_folder_watch.py`) started at daemon boot stat-walks configured `folder_watch.roots`, hashes on `(mtime,size)` change, settle-debounces (`quiet_debounce_s`) and min-interval-floors before enqueuing to the ingest queue (change detection opens no vault graph, so it scales past `max_open=8`). Live-run fixes: F1 — `ignore_dir_globs` (default `[".*", "__pycache__", "node_modules"]`, `DEFAULT_IGNORE_DIR_GLOBS`) prunes junk dirs before descent through one shared `_iter_watch_files` enumerator used by both the watcher and one-shot `POST /api/v1/ingest-folder` (the live run had 47% of Documents come from `.state/backups/` and `.remember/`); the `watch-folder add` request-key mismatch (`root` vs `path`) that 400'd every initial ingest is fixed. F2 — enqueue dedup: a still-queued path refreshes its durable copy + emits a `refreshed` event instead of a duplicate item, and `IngestItem.id` comes from a ServerState monotonic `ingest_seq` (seeded past every persisted id) rather than len()-based ids that collided after deletes. F4 — a `provider_error` with zero yield terminates as `status="error"` (visible, retryable) instead of a quiet `done`; retry accepts both error and done-with-provider-error items. F5 — the manifest sidecar withholds a pending edit (keeps the PRE-edit entry until enqueue is accepted) so a daemon restart inside the debounce window re-detects it. F11 — durable copies mirror the source tree (`sources/<sha256(root)[:16]>/<sanitized relpath>`) so a file's graph Document identity is stable and human-readable across edits. F12b/F13 recorded the historical ADR 0025 behavior in which non-active vault roots paused visibly because the v1 drain worker targeted the active vault; ADR 0034 supersedes that limitation, and every watcher now enqueues into its declaring immutable vault runtime whether or not a browser displays it. F12c — skipped non-text files surface as `skipped_non_text`. UI: a Folder Watch config section + live status panel + per-ingest event summaries, and superseded/detached badges on claims in the KG Browser. Historical v1 limitation (explicitly superseded by ADR 0034): the drain worker was active-vault-scoped; current source owns a drain worker per immutable vault runtime. pre-change claims carry no `asserted_at` so the recency prefilter cannot protect them (the merge judge remains the guard); no migration ships for the F11 identity change (demo-vault rebuilds from zero, other vaults heal via `kg rebuild`).

items.title: CLI-shell LLM providers — shared base + codex_cli + Validate/Test split
items.detail: A shared `CliShellProvider` Template Method base (`llm/_cli_provider.py`) factors the shell-out mechanics — message splitting, subprocess exec, timeout handling, usage-stat capture, and scoped cancellation — for all three local-binary LLM providers. `claude_cli` and `pi_cli` were retrofitted onto it, while `codex_cli` (the headless `codex` binary) was added on top. A companion Strategy pair in `llm/_structured_output.py` handles schema-constrained calls: `NativeSchemaStrategy` (trusts a CLI's own native schema flag — `claude --json-schema`, `codex exec --output-schema <file>` — one attempt, no repair) versus `BestEffortJsonStrategy` (`pi_cli`: embeds the schema as a prompt instruction, repairs the reply — fence-strip then balanced-brace extraction — and jsonschema-validates, reasking up to 3 attempts). `codex_cli` passes `model` verbatim to `-m` and never returns a model list from Validate (`codex --version` only) — Codex has no `models` subcommand and no model-catalog API, and an earlier version wrongly surfaced its `[model_providers.*]` config.toml endpoint keys as if they were models; live-testing proved passing one as `-m` fails, so Validate now just confirms the binary runs. A `CODEX_OBSERVER_DIR` env var is an opt-in debug sidecar (default off — unset means nothing is written): when set, every codex call writes a JSON record (command, model, prompt, output/schema paths, pid, timestamp) next to its output tempfile. Timeout handling reaps the whole process GROUP (POSIX `os.killpg` after `start_new_session=True`; Windows `taskkill /T /F`) instead of killing only the parent process, fixing an observed orphaned-child leak. The active-process registry also lets a scoped Stop Bulk Ingest request cancel the owning CLI process tree immediately rather than waiting for its timeout. The Config UI's per-provider probe split into two buttons: **Validate** (cheap reachability — CLI providers check the local binary / run subprocess model discovery instead of an HTTP probe) and **Test** (`POST /api/v1/llm/test-completion`, a real round-trip through the exact completion path every ask/ingest call uses, for every provider including all three CLI ones).

items.title: remember() stops lying about failure — honest provider errors, Windows paths, raw-text MCP ingest
items.detail: A live-use audit found `remember()` could report success while quietly extracting nothing. `RememberResult` gained three fields — `provider_failures` (count of blocks whose extraction call errored), `empty_after_retry_blocks`, and `llm_disabled` (true when `llm.enabled=false` skipped extraction entirely, structural-ingest-only, and is never conflated with a real failure) — and `remember()` now branches into three honest outcomes: (a) LLM disabled → structural-only, `llm_disabled=True`, never raises; (b) every attempted block failed (the 'has_heading-only' bug — a configured/reachable-looking LLM that silently extracted nothing) → the ledger run is marked `failed` and `Companion.remember()` raises `LLMUnavailableError` with the real provider error embedded, mirroring the ingest queue's F4 zero-yield rule; (c) partial failure (≥1 block succeeded) → returns normally with `provider_error`/`provider_failures` populated for caller-side visibility. REST `/remember` and MCP `remember` now surface that raised error as a real 500/tool-error instead of a silent 200 (`/api/v1/ingest` batch path is unchanged). Batch callers degrade gracefully instead of crashing: `kg rebuild` catches `LLMUnavailableError` per file, records it in a `failed_files` list, and keeps the structural content; the folder-watch runner catches it and re-queues the file to `incoming/` for retry rather than routing it to `failed/`. Two smaller fixes ride along: a Windows drive-letter path (`C:\Users\...`) is no longer misparsed by `urlparse` as an unsupported URL scheme (`c:`) in `Vault.add`'s source-scheme check; and MCP `remember` now accepts RAW TEXT as `source` (not just a path) — a multi-line string, or a single-line string with no path shape, is materialized to a new file under `.marginalia/sources/` before ingest, so the byte-range provenance the graph anchors to always has a real file behind it. Separately, `ask`'s `source_blocks_used` flag across every Tier-2/blend/escalation branch is now honest — it used to be `bool(rendered_context.strip())` (or unconditionally `True` on one branch), true even when the 'read' produced no real bytes; it's now `bool(actual_byte_reads and actual_byte_reads[0] > 0)`, true only when real source bytes survived the render budget.

items.title: Subgraph-first answer assembly (ADR 0011)
items.detail: Shipped as an opt-in graph-native path behind llm.ask.enable_subgraph; block answering remains the default. The north-star program refuted render-budget, ranking, and multi-hop knobs as the main ceiling and identified extraction recall as decisive. Efficient-hybrid source fallback shipped in v0.0.36; v0.0.37 union-k2 extraction plus retention fixes lifted extraction recall from 70.0% to 82.3%. Final validated A/B reached subgraph 122/142 versus block 120/142 (McNemar p=0.80) at 6.24x fewer context tokens, establishing parity with the accepted efficiency tradeoff. The implementation program is closed; residual monotonicity/model-floor/long-tail quality questions are future product backlog, not open work on this item or the corrective release gates.

items.title: Anchor LLM-extracted facts as Claims (not just edges)
items.detail: remember() now mints one byte-anchored Claim per extracted S-P-O relationship, anchored to its source Block and carrying confidence + model_id + prompt_hash — instead of bypassing the Claim/Block model with document-level edges. Pairs with unified retrieval: anchor on the way in, fuse on the way out. Verified end-to-end (recall "who is the partner on Marginalia?" → Jordan Lee Carter with byte provenance, 7 claims minted).

items.title: Provenance is a span, not a node — demote Block (ADR 0003)
items.detail: ADR 0003 landed additively: SourceSpan ships on Claims, fixed ~12k extraction windows replaced token-sized extraction fragments, provenance reads can use spans, and stored Blocks remain for compatibility and source-context recovery. The destructive 6-to-5 support-type cut and removal of Block/neighbor machinery were not accepted. Any future revisit is product architecture, not active implementation or a v0.0.40 release gate.

items.title: Claim→entity bridge edges — fuse the semantic & provenance layers (ADR 0005)
items.detail: The full-graph view exposed a structural defect: Claim provenance islands did not connect to their subject/object entities. ADR 0005 added idempotent rdf:subject/rdf:object bridges and source Document schema:mentions edges. The original bulk in-place `kg migrate bridge-edges` repair was later retired after it was proven to corrupt populated Ladybug adjacency (ADR 0007). New ingest mints bridges incrementally; existing vaults heal only by rebuilding from the markdown trust root into a fresh graph and atomically swapping it.

items.title: Source-link entities on primary ingest/rebuild paths — orphan root-fix (ADR 0006)
items.detail: ADR 0005 named schema:mentions (Document → entity) as a de-orphaning safety net but never wired it live, so 302 degree-0 orphan entities remained — 301 of them mention-only genuine entities carrying a source_path to a real Document that never got an edge. The fix makes schema:mentions node-derived through one shared ensure_source_mentions helper (iterate primitive-entity nodes by source_path, mint Document → entity, idempotent, type-allowlisted to the 5 primitives) and calls it in the primary remember() commit path after relationship-claim minting, so entities committed by ordinary ingest are source-linked at creation. Existing vaults heal through kg rebuild, which reuses the same helper rather than a parallel in-place patch; the earlier standalone kg migrate bridge-edges command was removed after bulk edge minting into an already-populated Ladybug graph was found to corrupt edge src/dst and adjacency (ADR 0007). Manual review-queue commits and automatic companion-triage commits currently use resolve_review() and do not invoke ensure_source_mentions, so this completed scope covers primary remember/rebuild paths rather than every possible node-commit path. A model-free regression guard asserts every sourced primitive entity has degree ≥ 1 after the helper. Pure edge addition, no schema change. Verified on the covered paths: ordinary ingest source-links sourced primitive entities, and rebuilding the existing vault dropped degree-0 sourced primitive entities 301 → 0.

items.title: Trust-root rebuild heal for bulk-migration edge corruption
items.detail: The 'rogue nodes' (~150 Claims reading as degree-0/1 orphans in the NX vault) were root-caused — after three walked-back theories (edge-id collision → read skew → 'any populated write') — to a storage-layer defect, using checks that cannot be contaminated by the bug (id-bound vs node-anchored reads, plus the markdown trust root). What is true: the content-addressed edge id is ground truth (markdown-verified, 1023/1023); the casualties are the stored src/dst scalars AND the FROM/TO adjacency; the corruptor is a BULK whole-store in-place migration pass (kg migrate bridge-edges / whole-store ensure_source_mentions) minting edges into an already-populated Ladybug graph — deterministic 0→1227 corrupted from 321 mints (it damages edges it never touched). It is NOT a write-Cypher-form bug (DELETE+CREATE / CREATE / MERGE / buffered all identical 0→1227), NOT a reader bug (full-scan agrees with id-bound on a clean vault), and incremental ingest / remember() is SAFE (+424 edges, 0→0). Fix (shipped, ADR 0007): kg rebuild now re-extracts the markdown trust root (.marginalia/sources/ + notes/refs) through the full remember() pipeline into a FRESH graph + atomic swap (rebuild-into-fresh is corruption-free), and the corrupting bulk migration is retired (the safe per-commit source-link is kept). Proven at full NX-vault scale on a copy: corruption 1227→0, adjacency/stored-prop mismatches 1680→0, degree-≤1 Claims 150→0, rich graph (2201 nodes / 8629 edges / 547 entities). The engine-internal cause and a content-addressed topology-edge scheme remain unscheduled upstream opportunities, not active Marginalia tasks or release gates.

items.title: Relation/Claim semantic identity + dedup (ADR 0016)
items.detail: Claim identity = the semantic triple (S, P, O); re-mentions corroborate one Claim (extra PROV edges + corroborations facet) instead of minting duplicates. Tier E0 within-run exact edge collapse, Tier E1 exact reconcile against the store, plain-edge commit guard, and a retroactive heal pass that collapses legacy duplicates and re-keys claims to semantic ids. Validated live: playground vault healed 3,180→3,021 claims (wrote_to 24-dup → 1 claim, corroborations 26), re-mention ingest minted 0 new claims with relations_corroborated=1.

items.title: Dedup aggressiveness tuning
items.detail: Open question: how confident before auto-merging two entities vs. linking them as related? Needs a calibrated threshold + authority-control path.

items.title: Retroactive same-type entity reconciliation
items.detail: SHIPPED v0.0.5 (ADR 0008). Consolidates already-committed look-alike entities that ingest-time resolution missed (e.g. 'Alex'/'Alex Rivera'/'Alex Jordan Rivera Blake'; 'taylor.nguyen'/'Taylor Nguyen'). Research-backed (SOTA entity resolution + KG canonicalization) and adversarially reviewed. Option A (default, ADR-0007-safe BY CONSTRUCTION): equivalence classes are skos:exactMatch (NOT owl:sameAs) stored OFF-GRAPH in .marginalia/authority/index.json and folded at READ time via search_claims and the Browse/Graph REST projections — ZERO graph writes (proven add_node==0 && add_edge==0, node/edge id-sets byte-identical), reversible by dropping the entry. Option B (periodic) physically folds confirmed aliases into a FRESH graph via kg rebuild. Recall lanes (widened embedding band + token-subset chain + email-handle decomposition; Jaro-Winkler as ordering not substring so Aler≠Mualer) funnel to the reused conservative LLMMergeJudge; auto-merge iff same AND conf≥0.9 AND per-variant corroboration, else queued (review-first safety net). Authority model wired (canonical_name→skos:prefLabel, variants→skos:altLabel). CLI: kg reconcile propose|apply|review|heal. E2E (real GLM, healed reference-vault copy): Alex 4→1 cluster (queued), Taylor merged, Aler/Mualer + NX/NX-Legal NOT merged, 0 false merges. Judge thinking-mode tuning remains an operational recommendation, not an open implementation task.

items.title: Review-queue UX — unified polling inbox
items.detail: The review-first Curation view unifies entity, predicate, and companion-candidate queues into one polling inbox with live count badges and explicit actions. Push notification remains an optional future enhancement, not unfinished review UX.

items.title: Local model floor + escalation policy
items.detail: Which local model is good enough for generic S-P-O extraction, and where/how do we escalate to a provider for non-sensitive content?

items.title: Content surfaces show knowledge, not plumbing
items.detail: Provenance/infrastructure nodes (system + LLM Agent/Activity) are excluded from recall, ask, and Browse through a durable mint-time marker. Raw Block substrate is excluded from untyped recall and ask, but remains visible in Browse's default All listing and support-type counts and can be selected explicitly, so operators can inspect the provenance substrate. Entity dedup is authority control: a note mentioning one entity twice now commits a single node, with edges remapped to the survivor (no dangling refs). Recall is question-aware: for interrogative queries it promotes the Claim that answers the question over the bare topic entity it is about. Markdown stays canonical throughout — provenance integrity fixes restored full byte-range claim_id citations on the read path without touching the vault. Named-title recall now has a bounded RRF title leg: multi-token titles whose terms are fully covered by the query (for example 'Alistair Cockburn User Story Format') receive a rank-domain signal, while one-word generic taxonomy nodes like 'Story' are left to the normal vector/lexical legs. One-hop graph expansion now target-degree-normalizes borrowed seed mass, so generic hubs cannot out-accumulate exact named hits merely because many candidate claims point at them.

subtasks.title: Filter provenance/infra from content surfaces and raw Blocks from untyped retrieval
Intra-batch entity dedup (authority control) before staging
Question-aware answer-Claim ranking (coverage-gated, deterministic)
Provenance integrity — byte-anchored citations on /query + drift envelope
Named-title recall leg for exact multiword concepts
Target-degree normalized graph expansion

items.title: Graph-expansion hub normalization + IDF-weighted answer ranking
items.detail: Two related ranking refinements, both now shipped on the 0.0.x line. Degree-normalized borrowed expansion mass prevents a dense topic hub from out-accumulating a genuine answer. Answer-Claim final-stage ranking is also shipped by default, unconditionally, on both retrieval paths. query._answer_ranked (query.py:92-125) detects an interrogative query, then computes IDF locally over the Claim candidate pool (BM25F-style df/idf over shared terms) and folds that IDF-weighted term-coverage score into the final answer-side reorder; a non-interrogative query yields an empty answer_ranked list, so the fold is a no-op and plain RRF ordering is unchanged — this closes the exact gap the original 'doing' text described (plain term-coverage with no term discrimination). subgraph._answer_coverage_scores (subgraph.py:180-211) ports the identical local-IDF computation into ego-graph bridge-claim selection, making it the PRIMARY sort key ahead of confidence when the degree_cap cut and render budget truncate candidates — so the Claim that actually answers the question survives instead of the highest-confidence generic sibling. Neither path sits behind a feature flag: query._answer_ranked is called directly inside retrieval assembly (query.py:470, 544) and subgraph._answer_coverage_scores runs inside seed/sibling ranking (subgraph.py:257, 686); both activate automatically whenever the query is interrogative, with no config toggle to opt in or out.

items.title: Extraction + cross-file resolution hardening (research #12)
items.detail: Shipped extraction, literal-Claim, naming/noise, within-batch, cross-file resolve, merge-judge, curator, ordered-model, practice-gate, and local-taxonomy hardening. Task 13 then raised strict extraction recall over 130 answerable questions from 70.0% to 82.3% through completeness-directed extraction and bounded candidate budgets; the final efficient-hybrid run answered 122/142 versus 120/142 for the full-token path while using 6.24x fewer context tokens. Residual tuning is future product work, not an active task or release gate.

items.title: CoP predicate and local taxonomy normalization
items.detail: A CoP live-ingest pass found two remaining quality defects after curator gating: literal Claim predicates kept local names such as uses_analogy, failure_mode, red_flag, constraint, recommended_view, tested_via, characterized_by, reduces_loop_time_from, and identifies_danger; and local taxonomy Concepts could enter as plural Epics, Stories, and Tasks. Relationship curation now falls back to canonicalizing the original extracted predicate when a commit verdict omits canonical_predicate, and normalize_predicate maps the observed CoP variants onto the preferred vocabulary: example, risk, constrains, recommended_approach, includes, describes, impact, and related canonical forms. parse_extraction also singularizes exact local taxonomy Concepts Epics/Stories/Tasks to Epic/Story/Task before ids and refs are minted.

items.title: CoP local taxonomy chain extraction
items.detail: A follow-up CoP audit found the inverse of the plural-normalization fix: the clean reingest no longer leaked Epics/Stories/Tasks, but it also did not propose the core Problem Decomposition chain nodes Epic, Story, and Task at all. The extraction prompt now has an explicit local taxonomy chain rule and exemplar for arrow/indentation hierarchies such as Epics -> Stories -> Tasks, telling the model to emit each unit as a Concept and the supported breaks_into relations before the curator gate. The relationship predicate fallback also maps generic has -> includes and has_condition/has_criterion -> requires so committed Task-to-criteria relations cannot leak non-vocabulary has-style edges.

items.title: CoP comparative literal integrity
items.detail: A follow-up CoP graph audit found a curator-approved but malformed comparative Claim: `Tooling Integration impact hours`, traced to extraction splitting the source fact `loop time drops from hours to minutes` into one-sided `reduces_loop_time_from=hours` and `reduces_loop_time_to=minutes` literals. Extraction now tells the model to keep comparative impacts as one full literal, and the relationship curator now queues one-sided comparative fragments such as only `hours` or only `minutes` when the source fact is a from/to comparison.

items.title: Extraction node hygiene — Claim un-extractable + generic-token denylist
items.detail: Two root-level fixes that stop the noisiest 'rogue node' classes at the source, born from a read-only diagnostic of the live NX vault. (1) Claim removed from ALLOWED_NODE_TYPES — a real claim is a propositional S-P-O fact that flows through the separate claims[] → EdgeCandidate channel, so listing Claim as an extractable node type only ever let the LLM emit a subjectless Claim-typed node; the title-name guard still drops a node literally titled 'Claim' (it no longer rides on allowlist membership). (2) A tiny conservative generic-token denylist drops bare file-type/format titles (pdf, doc, image, file, link, url) that the dense pipe-table files leaked as Concept/InformationObject nodes — membership-test only, never a length filter, so domain acronyms (NX, AI, ML, ZDR) always survive. Deeper extraction-prompt precision (generic single-word concepts, phrase fragments) is deferred.

items.title: ADR 0039 — Ingest technical correctness (integrity, fencing, durable resume)
items.detail: Accepted and implemented. Adds a graph-integrity auditor with a generation/fence sidecar, startup verification, a semantic-write fence, and the /api/v1/integrity surface, plus a framing-aware durable candidate-ledger resume behind a file lease and inode fence. A rebuild that fails validation stays fenced instead of installing a partial graph.

items.title: ADR 0040 — Semantic graph quality (proposed, evidence-gathering)
items.detail: Proposed, not accepted. Defines a fail-closed semantic acceptance matrix over four corpus classes with locked per-layer thresholds, exact scenario churn, byte grounding, review coverage, and ablations. Only the read-only diagnostic slice and the surface/identity evidence wiring have shipped; the acceptance collection is still incomplete, so no ADR 0040 acceptance claim may be made from any single corpus run.

items.title: Bi-temporal claims (valid-time vs transaction-time)
items.detail: Partial temporal semantics already ship: Claims carry source-recency asserted_at, and reconciliation stamps valid_as_of / valid_until for detach and supersede lifecycle. A complete bi-temporal model with first-class valid-time and transaction-time query semantics remains an unscheduled additive opportunity; it does not add a sixth primitive or block the current release.

items.title: Overdue-commitment / stale-head / authority-collision detectors
items.detail: All three closed-set detectors are implemented and wired in: commitment_temporal_shacl, supersedence_stale_head, authority_alias_collision (DETECTOR_NAMES, detectors.py:21-25). Runnable via CLI (cli/__init__.py:38 import, :1245 detector_names, :1792 run_detector dispatch), the REST/UI findings endpoint (server/http.py:40,1149), and the continuous-curation scheduler (server/_curation.py:927-933, runs all three per cycle). Regression-covered by tests/test_fr4_drift_fixtures.py.

items.title: Built SPA over the /api/v1 contract
items.detail: React + Vite + Tailwind + Zustand SPA (graph viz via @xyflow/react), served by the REST Starlette application on :7777. It talks to the store strictly through the locked /api/v1/* REST contract. REST/UI includes operator-only config, reset, and curation writes that are intentionally absent from the separate FastMCP tool surface. build.sh → frontend_dist/ mounted last with SPA fallback; ships as package data so wheel-install users get the UI.

subtasks.title: KG / database browser — closed-schema type facets, node detail with edges + byte-range provenance + 1-hop graph
Config panel — full LLM / embedder / gate / extraction control, applied:live|reembed, hard re-embed warning
Interactive query — recall + ask with answer text, citations, and byte-anchored source hits
Ingest view — paste / write / attach markdown → companion extraction → queryable knowledge; source persisted as the trust-root .md; loopback-only write
Allow-remote opt-in toggle (loopback-default base_url, env-name-only api keys)

items.title: ADR 0034 — direct browser application and tab-scoped multi-vault management
items.detail: The corrective source replaces the browser bootstrap/query-token/session-cookie ceremony with a plain loopback REST/UI application. `marginalia serve` opens the browser after readiness by default, `--no-open` is explicit headless mode, and startup requires no vault. Each tab selects its own vault and sends an explicit selector while immutable per-vault runtimes own jobs, queues, locks, schedulers, and watch drains, so switching never retargets permanent background work. The manager creates vaults and deletes only idle Marginalia-created vaults after exact-name confirmation; external, legacy, symlink-backed, leased, or busy vaults fail closed. The repository-owned Playwright smoke proves zero-vault launch, no cookie, independent tabs, switching while a durable curation job exists, managed embedding configuration, and guarded deletion against both source and an exact development wheel.

items.title: One managed credential flow for LLM and embedding providers
items.detail: LLM Defaults and Embedding now use the same loopback-only PUT /api/v1/credentials/provider contract for supported single-key providers. The browser sends the raw key once, receives only a generated MARGINALIA_PROVIDER_*_API_KEY reference, clears the password field, and saves only that reference to vault YAML. Provider or endpoint changes clear stale references. POSIX keeps the local secrets file owner-only; Windows stores managed values as CurrentUser-DPAPI envelopes so plaintext is absent at rest and a fresh process can recover the key. Credential chains and multi-field provider authentication remain on their provider-specific advanced environment flow.

items.title: Bulk & folder ingest — async background queue
items.detail: Beyond single paste/write: point at a local folder (server walks its own disk, loopback-only) or drag-drop a batch of files, and the companion drains them through one in-process worker per immutable vault runtime with a live per-file status poll. The blocking LLM extraction runs off the event loop via asyncio.to_thread so the poll and ordinary reads stay responsive; that runtime's writer lock still serializes its vault's writes one at a time and each store op opens its own Ladybug connection. The queue is now restart-durable: a metadata-only sidecar (.marginalia/ingest-history.json — never source content) is persisted best-effort on every state change via an atomic temp-file write and rehydrated on startup, so a server restart no longer loses the batch history; items left mid-flight (status processing) are treated as crash-interrupted and re-runnable since remember() re-anchors against the same byte-addressed source. The UI re-hydrates the queue on mount, so a browser refresh shows the live run instead of an empty board. Each processing item reports within-file progress — a stage label (Parsing → Extracting → Embedding → Dedup → Committing) plus blocks_done / blocks_total — so a large file shows motion instead of a frozen spinner. The queue snapshot now also carries blocks_total, nodes, edges, and claims per file; the Add page renders a selectable pipeline microscope with Parse/Chunks/LLM/Dedup/Commit stages, chunk bars, and per-file node/edge/claim/review metrics so the run shows what the document is becoming, not only whether it is queued. REST /add deterministic stores also record into /api/v1/ingest-queue as status=done stage=stored; the historical MCP kg_add tool was retired, and current MCP remember writes directly through the selected runtime's Companion/writer path rather than its browser bulk-import queue. The UI lifts the tab-selected vault's queue state app-level with one shared poller (1.2s active / 5s idle); every request carries the explicit vault selector, so work discovered in another tab cannot be conflated with another vault, and an 'Ingesting N/M' sidebar indicator shows from any view. Boot is hardened too: a corrupt Ladybug graph (kill -9 / torn-WAL) no longer crashes startup — bootstrap_vault_graph recovers in two tiers, preferring the last good checkpoint over a wipe. Ladybug only folds its WAL into the main graph.lbug checkpoint on a clean close, so a kill -9 mid-write usually tears just the WAL over an intact checkpoint; _recover_from_corruption now quarantines ONLY the torn WAL/sidecars (graph.lbug and marginalia's own graph.lbug.bak stay in place) and retries the open, recovering every claim in the last checkpoint (Vault.recovery_mode == "checkpoint") — proven live on a killed E2/E3 replay that would have silently dropped 5389 claims to 0 under the old wholesale-quarantine behavior. Only if the checkpoint itself is torn (no recoverable graph.lbug) does it fall back to the old path: quarantine everything into .marginalia/corrupt-graph/ and boot a fresh empty graph (recovery_mode == "empty"), logging a loud pointer to kg rebuild. /health now reports both recovered_from_corruption and a mode-accurate recovery_mode so the operator knows whether to just re-ingest recent sources or fully rebuild from markdown — the trust root is untouched either way. Trust-root preserved: pastes, uploads, AND folder files are all copied into .marginalia/sources/ under traversal-safe, path-hash-uniquified names, so everything the graph anchors to lives under the vault root that remember() re-validates. Per-file isolation (one bad file never kills the run), MAX_ENQUEUE=2000 + 2M-char upload caps. Loopback-only like config-write, even under --allow-remote.

items.title: Start fresh — wipe a vault (CLI · API · UI)
items.detail: A destructive reset that returns a vault to empty while keeping its identity. Three surfaces share one wipe_vault helper: the Web UI Config → Danger zone 'Start fresh' (confirm-gated), the CLI kg init <vault> --wipe (help: 'Wipe an existing vault (delete notes, sources, and the graph) then re-init'), and POST /api/v1/reset. A wipe deletes the derived graph, the durable ingest queue/history, and user content, then re-opens an empty vault — but marginalia.yaml (LLM / embedder / gate config) is preserved, so you start clean without re-configuring. Consistent with the rest of the mutating surface, the reset route is loopback-only: gated by the same remote_config_allowed check as config-write, so it is never reachable from a remote caller even under --allow-remote. The markdown trust root is the only true source — a wipe is the explicit way to discard it and rebuild.

items.title: Graph view — full-screen WebGL graph explorer
items.detail: A new top-level 'Graph' tab promotes graph exploration from the Browse view's one-hop mini-graph to a full-screen, zoomable WebGL explorer (sigma.js + graphology, ForceAtlas2 run on a worker so layout never blocks the UI). It is a pure read/visualization surface — no new write path, and it does not touch the ingest / resolution / remember() pipeline, the closed 5-primitive schema, the provenance model, or the confidence gates. Three new read-only REST routes back it, all under the locked /api/v1 contract. GET /api/v1/graph returns a capped, filtered OVERVIEW subgraph (never a raw dump): params types, relations, limit (default 1500, hard cap 5000), min_degree; it selects the top-`limit` nodes by in-filter degree, returns only edges whose both endpoints survive the cap, and flags `truncated` when the cap dropped nodes the filters kept — so a huge vault renders its densest core instead of erroring. GET /api/v1/nodes/{id}/neighbors (params hops 1–3, limit, types, relations) backs incremental click-to-expand from a seed node. GET /api/v1/graph/stats returns closed-schema node-type counts plus open-vocabulary edge-type counts, feeding the filter controls. The same content-vs-plumbing rule as recall/ask/Browse holds on the viz: closed-schema node types only and is_infra nodes excluded, so provenance/infra machinery never shows in the picture; unknown node-type filters 400, while edge relations are an open pack-defined vocabulary and pass through unvalidated. Type filters and a click-to-inspect detail panel sit over the canvas; an app-level ErrorBoundary and a WebGL-availability fallback in GraphView.tsx degrade gracefully when WebGL is unavailable.

items.title: Review-first Curation UX — Overview / Review inbox / Maintenance
items.detail: Curation page collapsed from 8 tabs to 3: Overview leads with a needs-your-decision hero (combined pending counts from the three review queues), a plain-language health line, and a heal nudge when confirmed decisions postdate the last heal; Review is one inbox (predicate folds, entity merges, node candidates) with live count badges; Maintenance hosts the demoted surfaces (heal/rebuild, authority audit, drift, manual reconcile). One shared attention hook polls the file-backed queue endpoints; the heavy vocabulary scan was moved off the event loop and cached after it froze the UI.

items.title: Web UI first-run wizard
items.detail: Related work from docs/installer-greenfield-onboarding-prd.md (2026-09-13): the Web UI owns default vault creation, selection, deletion, and provider setup but has no first-run wizard (docs/onboarding-plan.md, 2026-07-14: optional product UX backlog, not a release gate). When it ships, a greenfield user who declines the installer prompt gets an in-app path. Tracked separately from the v0.0.48 installer prompt; not a 0.0.48 item.

tracks.title: Curation control plane (Marginalia as an application)

items.title: P1 — Curation UI over existing endpoints
items.detail: Make invisible curation visible with ZERO new concurrency risk: SPA views over endpoints that already exist — detect-drift (POST /detect-drift) and the companion review queue (GET /review-queue + POST /resolve-review) — plus a Curation Dashboard tile over /graph/stats + /health. First executable review actions in the UI. (ADR 0009)

items.title: P2 — In-process curation job queue + reconcile/authority UI
items.detail: The spine: generalize server/_ingest_queue.py into a generic writer_lock-serialized job queue (daemon owns the one Ladybug handle → UI never goes down; a second process is the ADR-0007 corruption path). Expose reconcile propose/apply/review + authority records over new /api/v1/reconcile + /api/v1/authority with UI views (run/status, reconcile review queue, authority records with un-merge). Route the Browse list and graph overview through the equivalence fold so those aggregate views look deduped (closing the covered ADR-0008 UI gap). Focused node-neighborhood expansion remains raw/unfolded and can expose variant nodes. Off-graph only — no topology writes. (ADR 0009)

items.title: P3 — Topology-collapse heal (deterministic, in-process, reads-up)
items.detail: DONE: confirmed off-graph merges collapse the graph topology via a DETERMINISTIC graph->fresh-graph canonicalizing copy (NO LLM; reuse kg reembed scaffold + AuthorityIndex.equivalence_map): drop variant nodes, remap edges to canonical, recompute content-addressed ids, dedup, drop self-loops, remap Claim S_id/O_id. Runs as an in-process curation job; READS STAY UP for the whole copy (writer_lock held, no mark_draining; draining scoped to the sub-second swap). Fast (~3min vs a rejected ~4hr full-LLM re-extraction). Fresh-graph-safe (ADR-0007), reversible (kg rebuild re-derives from markdown). E2E: 2350->2326 nodes, 0 corruption, reads 798/798=200 during copy, mid-heal /add not lost. 106 tests pass. (ADR 0009)

items.title: P4 — Continuous curation loop + scheduler
items.detail: DONE: a debounced in-process scheduler (server/_scheduler.py) auto-runs reconcile-propose + detect-drift sweeps as ingestion proceeds — PROPOSE/DETECT ONLY (code-constant allowlist; never auto-applies a destructive/irreversible op, mirrors ADR 0009 invariant). Debounced off in-process ingest activity (last_ingest_at) + min-interval floor + coalesce (burst→one sweep). Config CurationSchedulerConfig (enabled/quiet_debounce_s/min_interval_s, conservative defaults). Surfaced at GET /api/v1/curation/scheduler + the Curation Dashboard. Reads stay up (writes=False sweep jobs); cancellable on shutdown. E2E: auto-sweep fires after ingest, burst coalesces to 1, 0 destructive auto-jobs, reads 200 throughout, disable-toggle stops it, SIGTERM-cancellable, no corruption. Tests pass. (ADR 0009) Historical multi-vault follow-up (2026-07-10): the scheduler expanded from the one active REST/UI vault to the active vault UNION open MCP-pool paths. ADR 0034 supersedes that intermediate design: the process supervisor iterates immutable vault runtimes, and each runtime owns its scheduler debounce, ingest timestamp, sweep timestamp, job queue, and locks. Browser selection is irrelevant; every configured runtime continues independently, while `VaultPool.paths()` remains a lock-free health/ownership snapshot.

items.title: P5 — Autonomy policy + observability
items.detail: Per-operation static CurationPolicy (operation × autonomy level + thresholds, mirroring per-step LLMConfig) evaluated as the gate; COMPILED invariant that irreversible/topology-minting ops never reach full-auto (reversibility sets defaults). Autonomy Config view + data-observability dashboard (freshness/volume/distribution/integrity/lineage). ADR 0013 now defines the lineage substrate for ingestion-time curation: durable candidate records, comparisons, commit plans, and commit records. (ADR 0009 + ADR 0013)

items.title: P6 (optional) — in-graph fold + MCP curation tools
items.detail: Gated by a decision fork: collision-safe edge-id rebuild to enable TRUE in-graph equivalence folding (closes ADR-0008 at the data layer, not just the UI); revive curation MCP tools into the running runtime.py MCP; later — overturn-rate self-tuning, bi-temporal invalidate-not-delete, small-LM cost tier. (ADR 0009)

items.title: Judge-driven continuous graph upkeep — predicate canonicalization (ADR 0017)
items.detail: Recurring upkeep loop: predicate vocabulary is embedding-clustered, candidate pairs judged by a bias-mitigated LLM (multi-option same/inverse/narrower/distinct verdicts, symmetric prompting, evidence-grounded), decisions persisted as SSSOM-shaped alias records in .marginalia/predicates/aliases.json with a negative cache, folds applied at ingest (normalize_predicate vault table), query time, and heal time (with claim title recompose); scheduler proposes continuously (propose-only per ADR 0009), auto-fold gated at 0.85 confidence, inverse/narrower always queue for human review. Validated live: 30 pairs judged on the playground vault, 17 auto-folds (e.g. reported_symptoms→reported_symptom), heal materialized 40 predicate folds with display names recomposed.

items.title: Judge triage + batch actions for the node-candidate review queue
items.detail: The companion review queue (extraction candidates the ingest curator declined) is no longer a manual pile: a companion-triage job re-judges queued candidates in batches with graph context (established-entity correlation), auto-commits verdicts that clear the same 0.75 ingest gate, auto-discards confident noise, and keeps only genuine borderliners; live judging and apply progress stream to the job. The Review inbox gains type/confidence filters, select-all, and bulk commit/discard via POST /review-queue/batch. Validated live: 1,703 queued candidates triaged to 382 committed / 1,259 discarded / 62 kept, 0 errors.

items.title: Conditional greenfield onboarding prompt in the public installer
items.detail: Specified in docs/installer-greenfield-onboarding-prd.md (proposed, 2026-09-13). A greenfield (no vault or config under ~/.marginalia) interactive TTY install gets a one-shot prompt: "Marginalia first run: no vault configured. Set up your vault and LLM provider now? [Y/n] (default Y)" — Y runs the existing signed-off `marginalia onboard` flow (the user names their own vault in-flow), n/EOF falls through to the current application-first path with a one-line `marginalia onboard` hint. Non-TTY/CI, MARGINALIA_NO_OPEN=1, MARGINALIA_VAULT preseed, the new --no-onboard flag (with marginalia-dist/test-install.sh scenario parity), and reinstall/upgrade all never prompt; the preseed path stays byte-identical, the installer still invents no vault, and the prompt is greenfield-only so upgrades never nag. Shipped in v0.0.48 (dist 5e5cd95) exactly as specified, and install.ps1 was intentionally untouched (the PRD is silent on Windows).

items.title: Remove the stale Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ4-fp16-mtp default model
items.detail: Companion item in docs/installer-greenfield-onboarding-prd.md §7. Implemented 2026-09-13 (ships in v0.0.48), per the PRD's recommended option 1 — empty default with discovery-first: LLMDefaults.model now defaults to empty (src/marginalia/config/_vault.py), so /api/v1/config/defaults on a fresh ~/.marginalia returns an empty model instead of the stale hardcoded name; the hidden legacy-local onboarding preset (src/marginalia/onboarding.py) carries no model, so the flow runs its existing discovery step against the base URL (pick-list from the provider's model endpoint, manual entry only as the fallback); the Web UI mock (frontend/src/lib/mock.ts) and the rebuilt bundle carry no model. The 0.0.47 state the fix removes: the string sat at src/marginalia/config/_vault.py:830, src/marginalia/onboarding.py:214, and the built bundle (frontend_dist/assets/index-C7q9NrnC.js), while the loopback endpoint 127.0.0.1:8123 lists Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.8-Flash, bge-m3, … and does not serve it. A real current model name was rejected: the same staleness failure would recur for every future endpoint change.

items.title: P1 — Eval harness first (Tier A) + judge instrumentation (M1)
items.detail: Measurement before behavior change. Land the real-fixture, no-LLM Tier A gold-set gate (tests/reconcile/test_recall_gold.py) and surface DISTINCT judge reasons in _pairwise. String-deterministic recall/precision cells are hard gates (Tovrin subset, NX-Lab surname collision, taylor.nguyen handle); embedding-dependent cells (Alex, Aler/Mualer) are measured against RECONCILE_RECALL_FLOOR; RED-today gaps (Nivod/Ari Nivod, Tovereign pollution) are xfail(strict) so they flip to hard gates the instant P2 lands. M1 makes the '26/28 empty reason' artifact a real, measurable judge-engagement signal. (ADR 0010)

items.title: P2 — Candidate recall + de-pollution (Axis 1)
items.detail: Close the under-merge: order-insensitive token_subset_unordered (a proper token-set subset sharing a distinctive token, dropping the shared-first-token requirement) so Nivod/Ari Nivod co-cluster and reach the judge; length-gate the short-token fuzzy lexical edge so Tovereign (jaro_winkler 0.922) is no longer welded into the Tovrin merge cluster. Verifiable by the Tier A xfail cells flipping to XPASS. No honorific gazetteer. (ADR 0010)

items.title: P3 — Corroboration unification + distinguishing-edge veto (Axis 3)
items.detail: Replace boolean _variant_corroborated with one graded signal — identity-grade (token containment / handle decomposition), relational (neighbour Jaccard), fuzzy-supporting (never sufficient alone) — so corroborated_ids keeps identity/relational and excludes fuzzy-only. Add the negative tier: a distinguishing edge (distinguished_from / different_from / not_same_as — alias_of denotes sameness and is excluded) subtracts a member the judge wrongly merged. NX Lab/Tamola never enter corroborated_ids; taylor.nguyen stays identity-grade; Tovereign drops to fuzzy. (ADR 0010)

items.title: P4 — Judge prompt exemplars + cluster-path enable_thinking (Axis 2: M3, M4)
items.detail: Two scoped exemplars in _VERDICT_SYSTEM: a bare name that is a token-subset of a fuller name with no conflicting surname is SAME (Tovrin/Tovrin Kalia), holding the 'two different full names sharing a first name' line DISTINCT; a team/org-unit vs a person bearing a related name is DISTINCT (NX Lab vs Luke Gray). Forward enable_thinking into _try_cluster_judge so the optional cluster path stops running at provider-default thinking. (ADR 0010)

items.title: P5 — Tier B band gate (Axis 5, laptop-only)
items.detail: K-run real-judge harness scoring must-merge / must-distinct RATES against bands, plus a hard ==0 auto-merge guard on NX Lab/Tamola across all K on both judge paths, with FRESH authority/queue side-files per K iteration (a persisted upsert corrupts the rate denominator). Laptop-only, never CI. (ADR 0010)

items.title: P6 — Judge abstain (M2) + shared-neighbour recall lane (deferred, gated)
items.detail: Deferred until P1's instrumentation gives a real disengagement rate. A reason-required abstain disposition routing non-engaged gold-class pairs to the review queue (carries the mandatory apply.py skip-branch fix so same=False-with-review-members is not silently dropped), plus the shared-neighbour recall lane that co-considers Alex R./Alex M. with relational context. Identifier-based Alex auto-merge stays out of scope until the Agent→Identifier ingest path lands (Q1). (ADR 0010)

items.title: Automated recall-quality and provenance eval harness
items.detail: Deterministic, CI-safe direct-Vault eval over a fixed synthetic vault: asserts entity presence at k, byte-range provenance, and partner recall. Acceptance scenario 92 drives the direct-loopback /api/v1/recall endpoint end to end and deliberately never probes an ambient LLM endpoint; live extraction and answer quality belong to explicit real-model scenario 56. General HTTP response shapes, pagination, config round-trips, and closed-schema type-filter validation are covered separately by ordinary server API tests; they are not the scope of pytest -m eval.

items.title: One laptop quality gate over three tiers
items.detail: A single laptop command consolidates the eval surface. Tier 0 re-runs the unchanged CI deterministic floor in-process for parity and aborts everything below on failure. Tier 1 starts a suite-owned daemon on an isolated home and vault, live-ingests the six semantic-adversarial documents so an extraction regression is actually visible, and gates citation byte-verification, hard-recall@k, extraction-completeness, deterministic must_contain, and negative-control abstention on counts against a committed baseline. Tier 2 records the reference-guided semantic judge as an advisory band that can never fail the gate; it hardens into a gate only after a measured kappa of at least 0.60 against human labels is committed. The Tier 1 baseline is PROVISIONAL: it was minted while ADR 0040 adjudication was still open and re-mints when that closes, so a pass today means no regression against a tree with known open findings rather than proven quality.

items.title: Config-write + query security-hardening gate
items.detail: Exercises the SSRF allowlist (loopback-only base_url unless allow_remote), http/https scheme + numeric-range rejection, env-name-only API keys, and the byte-read path re-validation on recall/ask before any source span is exposed. Historical immutable-0.0.40 evidence covered a single-use browser bootstrap and cookie; ADR 0034 supersedes that browser-authentication contract. Current source serves REST/UI directly on literal loopback with no browser credential, bootstrap, query token, or cookie, while enforcing the loopback Host allowlist, same-origin/Fetch-Metadata write checks, JSON content types, no permissive CORS, and frame denial. FastMCP alone retains an application-scoped bearer capability on its separate port. Direct non-loopback server startup fails closed even with the compatibility `--allow-remote` flag; remote operators use an SSH tunnel to the loopback listener. Config writes (`PATCH /api/v1/config`, folder-watch roots) use the selected runtime's dedicated `config_lock` so Save is never queued behind a multi-minute in-flight ingest; curation review actions (reconcile confirm/reject, predicate-upkeep confirm/reject, authority unmerge) still need that runtime's `writer_lock` for correctness but use `_writer_lock_fast` (5s timeout → `503 busy`) instead of blocking indefinitely; `GET /api/v1/detect-drift` does not take `writer_lock` because every detector is read-only.

items.title: Interactive UI validation checklist
items.detail: Manual checklist over the seven-view UI (Query, Add, Logs, Browse, Graph, Curation, Config) against a live vault: browse/inspect provenance, config round-trip with applied semantics + re-embed warning, queue/log visibility, graph/curation reads, and recall/ask source-span rendering.

items.title: Two-vault live ingest quality guardrail
items.detail: A repeatable HTTP-level guardrail validates agentic ingest across intentionally different SDLC and literary vaults. It separates graph plumbing from knowledge nodes, checks isolated knowledge, extracted and active-ledger candidate counts, accepted pre-commit size, domain-profile coverage, noisy predicates, type instability, and compact queue evidence. The guardrail drove generic table/list, cited-work, physical-artifact, predicate, duplicate-survivor, and relationship-liveness fixes. Historical live-run counts are evidence snapshots rather than a claim that one old ingest is still active.

items.title: 2026-09-03 deep-review remediation (32 findings)
items.detail: An independent deep review reproduced 32 confirmed findings against the live code, from critical (the acceptance harness's finish() reporting PASS when a scenario's server never started) through high (predicate-judge canonical-label normalization, Tier-0 store-reconciliation edge-endpoint guard, cross-directory Block id collision, un-retired stale deterministic claims, silent curator-timeout no-op) to medium and low severity (chunk-overlap duplicate claims and block-count blowup, non-transitive edge-endpoint guards, brace-tracking JSON extraction, legacy-route k cap, resolve-review loopback gate, InMemoryStore/LadybugStore parity, prompt-injection framing on extraction/judge prompts, sensitivity enum validation, argv system-prompt leakage, and further low-severity hygiene items). Every finding was fixed with a scoped commit and live validation (regression tests, reproductions, or model-free gate runs) rather than deferred; findings judged not currently exploitable or already self-healing were fixed anyway for defense in depth and recorded as such rather than left open.

items.title: Unified knowledge base + documentation hub
items.detail: Curated reading surface: every registered durable source in the explicit scope (root README and RFC files plus docs/) is rendered and themed, with instruction files, tests, generated assets, scratch state, and other declared exclusions kept outside the product knowledge base. The separately maintained Understanding walkthrough is linked and independently verified.

items.title: Living roadmap board + timeline (this view)
items.detail: Structured roadmap.json renders the Done/Doing/Next/Later board and milestone timeline. Reconciled 2026-07-13 against live source, ADR, release, distribution, and test state; future product backlog is explicitly distinct from release gates.
